Urinalysis & Urine Culture - Summary Table 
PAS 673: Introduction to Clinical Year II - Winter 2026 
Indications for Urinalysis 
Indicated   Not Indicated 
Signs/symptoms of acute infection
Reduction of GFR (acute or chronic) / AKI
Check for albuminuria
Suspected kidney disease (PE findings, comorbidities)
Monitoring / progression / staging of CKD
Asymptomatic screening before urologic procedure 
Gross Assessment 
Finding   Normal   Causes / Differential
Color   Clear, light yellow   Red to brown:   hemoglobin, myoglobin, RBCs 
Medications:   rifampin, phenytoin 
Foods:   beets, rhubarb, food dyes 
Turbidity   Clear   Infection, genital secretions, crystals, cells 
Odor   Mild / aromatic   Pungent / ammonia:   infection, retention 
Fruity:   ketones (DKA, starvation)

-

suctioning; renal tubular acidosis (some types) 
Decreased (acidic):   metabolic acidosis; DKA;
starvation; diarrhea; kidney failure
- 
Heme   Negative (trace /
small / mod / large)
Bladder cancer; kidney stone; UTI;
glomerulonephritis; trauma; rhabdomyolysis;

recommended

Protein (albumin)   Negative
Mod albuminuria
30-300 mg
Severe >300 mg

-   -

-   Products of fat metabolism, not normally in urine

-   -

(>2.0 elevated)
Hemolysis / hemolytic anemia; hepatocellular

Antibiotic suppression of gut bacteria; bile duct

End product of conjugated bilirubin metabolized by

Microscopic Examination 
Centrifuge 10-15 mL fresh urine; transfer one drop to slide with cover slip. Identify casts, cells, crystals, and bacteria. 
Element   Normal   Significance / Causes
Erythrocytes (RBCs)   0-3 RBCs / HPF   Confirm with dipstick heme. Transient vs persistent. Glomerular vs nonglomerular causes - assess morphology (dysmorphic =
glomerular) 
Leukocytes (WBCs)   Men: <2 WBC/HPF
Women: <5 WBC/HPF
Pyuria - infection, inflammation; correlate with LE and nitrite 
Epithelial cells   Few   Squamous:   contamination 
Renal tubular:   tubular damage 
Casts   Hyaline casts may be normal   Cylindrical shape reflects tubule of formation; localizes disease to a specific GU site (e.g., WBC casts   →   upper tract / pyelonephritis) 
Crystals   Variable   Type depends on urine pH and underlying disease (uric acid, calcium oxalate, struvite, cystine) 
Bacteria   None   Gram-negative rods, streptococci, staphylococci - correlate with culture 
When to Examine the Urine Sediment 
Should examine   Could examine   Unnecessary 
Clarify findings on dipstick
AKI
Initial work-up of undifferentiated CKD
Follow-up of acute and chronic kidney disease
Initial evaluation of kidney stones
Negative dipstick + mildly impaired renal function
DM with mildly impaired kidney function and albuminuria

Urine Culture & Sensitivity 
Topic   Detail
Positive culture   >100,000 CFU/mL = positive. 1,000-100,000 CFU/mL may indicate UTI in symptomatic patients. 
MIC   Minimum Inhibitory Concentration - lowest antibiotic concentration that prevents visible bacterial growth 
Appropriate uses   Symptoms suggestive of UTI   (except healthy nonpregnant young females with typical acute simple cystitis) 
New onset / worsening sepsis without another source
Fever or altered mental status without another source 
Inappropriate uses   Odorous, cloudy, or discolored urine without other localizing signs/symptoms
Reflex cultures based on UA findings (e.g., pyuria) without other indications
Documenting response to therapy (unless symptoms fail to resolve) 
Case Summary 
Case   Patient   Key Findings   Diagnosis / Management
#1   22F, dysuria, urgency, frequency, suprapubic
pressure; no fever / CVA tenderness
Cloudy urine; LE ++; nitrite +; 15-20 WBCs/hpf; moderate
bacteria 
Acute uncomplicated cystitis 
Empiric outpatient therapy; culture often not required in healthy nonpregnant
young female with typical symptoms 
#2   75M with BPH (tamsulosin), worsening
hesitancy, dribbling, fever 100.8°F, dark/foul
urine
Turbid; LE +++; nitrite +; >50 WBCs/hpf; many bacteria; PVR
250 mL; WBC 12,500 
Complicated UTI   (male + obstruction/retention)
Urine culture; broad-spectrum antibiotics; address retention 
#3   26F, 22w gestation; chills, N/V, R flank pain; T
102.4°F; tachycardic; +CVA tenderness
Turbid 'meat-wash'; LE +++; nitrite +; packed WBCs;   WBC
casts ; gram-neg rods; WBC 16k w/ left shift 
Acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy 
Admit; IV antibiotics; fetal monitoring; culture-guided therapy 
#4   24F, 12w gestation, asymptomatic; routine
prenatal screening
Culture: 100,000 CFU/mL E. coli; LE trace; nitrite +; 5-10
WBCs/hpf 
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy 
Treat   (unlike non-pregnant adults) to reduce risk of pyelonephritis and
preterm labor
